questions.question: A memory says 'the physician has a clinic on weekdays'. The user asks to 'see a doctor'. Why does keyword search miss it?
options: The memory is too old
The two texts share no words, so a word-matching method scores them as unrelated
Keyword search is case-sensitive
The query is too short
questions.explanation: Matching meaning rather than words is what embeddings are for.

questions.question: Why is cosine similarity used to compare embeddings, rather than raw distance?
options: It is faster to compute than anything else
It compares direction and ignores length, so a short query and a long document about the same thing can still match
It always returns integers
Providers require it
questions.explanation: Length mostly reflects how much text there is; direction reflects what it is about.

questions.question: Which embedder handled the typo 'restaurnt', and why?
options: TF-IDF, because it weights rare words
Character 3-grams, because the typo still shares most 3-letter pieces with 'restaurant'
PPMI, because it learned synonyms
None of them
questions.explanation: PPMI and TF-IDF work on whole words, and 'restaurnt' is a word neither has seen.

questions.question: How did PPMI learn that 'car' and 'automobile' are similar?
options: From a dictionary of synonyms
Both words appeared near the same context words (engine, mechanic, drive) in its training corpus
From their spelling
By asking an LLM
questions.explanation: Words used in similar contexts get similar vectors. Remove those sentences and the similarity disappears.

questions.question: You switch your memory store to a new embedding model. What must you do with the vectors already stored?
options: Nothing; vectors are compatible across models
Re-embed all stored texts with the new model, because vectors from different models are not comparable
Average the old and new vectors
Only re-embed the newest memories
questions.explanation: Each model defines its own space. Store which model made each vector.

questions.question: How should you choose an embedding model for your agent's memory?
options: Pick the top of a public leaderboard and stop
Build a small labelled test from your own data (exact, typo, paraphrase queries) and compare candidates on it
Pick the one with the most dimensions
Pick the cheapest
questions.explanation: Leaderboards are a starting point; your queries and documents decide what works.
